comments.author: ER_BoY
comments.body:
Looks impressive, but a few things make me skeptical:



1. Everything is "before fees". At \~1,300 trades a day, fees, spread and slippage are basically the whole game. What does it look like after costs?



2. It's running in SHADOW mode with pretend orders. With penny stocks that's a huge difference. In a simulation every order fills at your price. In reality you're in a queue, the price moves away, or you get filled worse.



3. The average profit is about $0.15 per trade ($3.5k / 23k trades) on thousands of shares. One cent of slippage per trade and the edge is gone.



4. An 85% win rate with tiny wins is classic "picking up pennies in front of a steamroller". One halt or sudden drop can wipe out weeks.



Not saying it can't work, but I'd want to see it live with real money, after fees, before trusting it. Curious to see the real results if you switch it to LIVE.

comments.author: spoidercide
comments.body:
Your strategy's profit structure stands on a needle with this risk structuring.

It's possible it can be tuned in the direction of being profitable.  
But even at 0.05 cents per fill you'd be at 1/3rd the profit and at 0.10 cents you're already down 1k.

Without fees, spread confirmation, or slippage this can't be taken at face value.  
Typical U.S. OTC penny-stock commissions range from $0 to $6.95 per order at major retail brokers.

What brokerage and execution model is this using, and does that P&L account for bid-ask spread and slippage?

I encourage everyone to use AI to help themselves learn but you have let it do all the cooking for you without learning the basic fundamentals of quantitative finance.

Ask your AI what you're not accounting for next time before you get too excited and blow up an account with a strategy that has only 1 extremely weak walk forward speculative model in an extremely short time frameto show anything for.

Turn 18 days into weeks or months and you could have something. 18 Days might as well be 18 hours in this industry. Trading algorhythms are meant to be commissioned and maintained with a robust confidence they can outlast at least an entire regime spanning several weeks to months or even years depending on the model.

This is HFT and if you attempt high frequency trading for your first strategy I promise you without the necessary experience you will get absolutely cooked.

This type of model can also work with crypto currencies if you're willing to learn the other half of that industry and get the appropriate hardware and datastreams for <30 second fills live.

You are entering one of if not the oldest most competitive industries in the world and as soon as your money is in the market you are competing with the best there is and its the big leagues and there is no in between. It's you vs institutionalized market makers who have been making algos in universities with super computers and AI several times more advanced than what an average person has available to them or could afford.

You have definitely achieved something here and you are right to be proud. Your work is very far from over still and do not give up.

Rule #1 is always account for up to double your average cost in fees to account for slippage or your strategy realistically stands no chance until those are calculated.
